learnerSourceCheck.prompt: In the source Noah paints a wall 6 metres wide and 3 metres high. How many square metres?

supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceGoal: Solve area problems in a community garden
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceLearningGoals: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area.
teachingSteps: Calculate each Number Talk expression mentally; explain what one extra group changes.
Use a labelled wall diagram to find square-meter area, then compare several sufficient paint purchases.
Garden first read: discuss the situation. Second read: identify the quantities. Keep the questions closed until the third read.
On the third read, open the garden tasks, create a labelled poster, and compare group strategies in a gallery walk.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.caution: Do not turn the source paint-buying or garden-design tasks into one numeric target; costs/prices are not specified. Square meters and square feet are not interchangeable.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.targetRichV2Field: 2021 source-specific canonical Rich V2 bridge authored

firstPartyPractice.prompt: Extra Edulytics question with an added condition: use ONLY containers covering 10 m² each to paint an 18 m² wall. What is the minimum number? This is different from the open source purchase-choice task.

independentEdulyticsCoolDown.prompt: New Edulytics planter: one side is 2 ft and the area must be at least 12 ft² but no more than 18 ft². Give ONE possible other side, with ft, and explain your choice. Whole numbers, decimals and fractions may be used.

stageC.humanRubric: Source-informed rubric: check equal-group strategies; 6 m × 3 m = 18 m²; accept any non-negative whole-container purchase covering at least 18 m² with sizes 3/10/40 m², without invented prices or a minimum-can restriction. Keep garden side 3 ft and area 20–30 ft² inclusive. Whole-foot other sides 7/8/9/10 ft work; other feasible measured lengths also work. Review units, drawings, coherent explanations, an organized poster, a description of another group strategy and THREE specific gallery observations. MLR8 annotated rows/columns, MLR6 Three Reads, inch tiles, centimeter grid paper as a scale model, visual-display tools and equitable group roles are authored. Numeric feasibility never proves classroom participation or teacher sign-off.
